stories.title: Startup uses motion sensors and AI to tell families when an aging parent’s routine changes
stories.summary: A Bellevue startup called Thessai is using motion sensors and AI — no cameras, microphones, or wearables — to learn an aging parent's daily routine and flag when something's off. Founder Michael Nassirian built it after his mother-in-law fell and told no one until the next day.
stories.extended_summary: Michael Nassirian's mother-in-law fell at home and had a phone and emergency button within reach — but she didn't use them, and didn't tell anyone until the next day when she needed an ambulance. That silence, he learned, is common: older adults say 'I'm OK,' don't want to be a bother, and above all don't want to advertise a fall. So Nassirian, a former Microsoft HoloLens exec, bought motion sensors at Home Depot and wrote software to alert his wife if her mother stopped moving. That became Thessai, a system that learns a person's normal patterns and flags anything unusual — all without cameras, microphones, or wearables seniors tend to refuse.
